segments.text: How can a square on a label hold a message? Look closely at a QR code. Its light and dark squares form a grid, with information arranged across rows and columns.
First, the scanner finds three large corner patterns. They show where the code is and which way it faces. Alternating timing marks help the scanner line up with the little squares.

Once it has the grid, the reader can interpret the encoded data. Some of those squares carry extra information for error correction, which can help recover a message even if part of the code is damaged.
